title: I Took the Groomer-Crate Log to the Desk Who Swapped My Dog

parts.text: I tagged crate 6 at 11:18 a.m. and desk Pio had already moved my dog to an unsigned overflow. The sheet said: CRATE ON THE TAG. NO SWAPS. PHOTO THE COLLAR. I was forty, client, holding a collar photo. Pio shrugged. "Desks are the floor." I photographed the sheet, the overflow, and my tag on empty 6. Then I asked for the crate log. At 11:24 the owner pinged why Pio's name was on a swap. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner can see Pio's unsigned overflow with my collar photo still on crate 6.

social.video_title: The desk swapped my dog off the tagged crate — Part 1/2
social.description: Groomer, a crate tag, an unsigned overflow. I logged the swap. Would you have asked the owner?

parts.text: Pio called it flow until the owner asked for the still. I printed the log, the sheet, and the photo. My dog went back to 6. Pio ran tags like everyone else and told the next desk flow was always about optics. Optics is a word desks use when collars exist. Log policy now has a second line: DESKS DO NOT SWAP. I keep crate 6. Pio brown-bags the jokes. The floor finally looks like a tag, not a shuffle. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Crate log, dog back on 6, and a second line. Was flow ever my collar?
